core_philosophy.design_principle: Single source of truth. Every transaction flows through one integrated system — no data silos between departments. Accounts, Stock, Manufacturing, HR are not bolt-ons, they are one system.
core_philosophy.target_mindset: Companies willing to adapt their processes to system discipline. ERPNext rewards structure. Companies that want 'ERP to work how we work' will struggle unless their processes are already reasonably well-defined.
core_philosophy.flexibility_vs_structure: High structure, medium-to-high flexibility. Out-of-box covers 85% of MSME needs. Remaining 15% customizable without touching core (via hooks, custom fields, custom doctypes). Core rarely needs forking.
core_philosophy.customization_philosophy: Configure first (custom fields, custom print formats, workflows). Script second (server-side scripts, client scripts). Code only when unavoidable (custom apps, hooks). Philosophy: don't break upgrade path.
core_philosophy.indian_dna: ERPNext was built in India, for Indian businesses first. GST, e-Invoicing, e-Way Bill, TDS, PF/ESI are first-class citizens — not afterthoughts. This is a fundamental advantage over SAP/Oracle for Indian MSME market.
core_philosophy.community_model: Large open-source community. 15,000+ GitHub stars. 1,000+ contributors. Active forum (discuss.frappe.io). Indian partner ecosystem of 500+ certified implementers. Community solves problems fast.

digital_maturity.description: Company uses computers, email, possibly Tally/Excel. Not paper-only. Owner or at least one staff member can learn software with training.

levels.level_1: Paper-only, no computers (too early for ERPNext)
levels.level_4: Custom legacy system (complex migration, but possible)

process_maturity.description: Company has some defined processes, not totally ad-hoc. Owner can describe how they work. Invoices exist. Purchase orders sometimes raised.
process_maturity.if_below_level_2: Extensive process consulting needed before ERPNext. ERPNext won't fix undefined processes — it will just automate the chaos.

ideal_customer_profile.owner_profile: Owner understands that ERP requires discipline, not just software. Willing to enforce process changes on team. Has identified at least one internal champion.
ideal_customer_profile.technical_profile: No in-house IT required for usage. Implementation partner handles setup. 1-2 staff can learn system admin basics for day-to-day management.

functional: End-to-end integrated ERP — Accounts, Stock, Sales, Purchases, Manufacturing, HR, Projects all in one system. No integration needed between modules.
Manufacturing depth — BOM, Work Order, Job Card, Routing, Workstation, Subcontracting, Quality Inspection. Covers discrete, job shop, and process manufacturing.
India compliance — GST (CGST/SGST/IGST/CESS), e-Invoicing (IRN), e-Way Bill, TDS, TCS, PF, ESI, professional tax. All built-in, not add-ons.
Project-based costing — Native Project module with cost tracking (material + labor + overhead per project). Excellent for job shops, fabrication, services, construction.
Batch and serial tracking — Full lot-based traceability for food/pharma. Serial number tracking for electronics/equipment. FIFO/FEFO enforcement.
Item Variants — Size/color/grade variants without separate item codes. Template + Attribute system. Critical for garment, hardware, footwear industries.
Subcontracting — Material transfer to job worker tracked. Goods received from subcontractor. Material accountability maintained.
Multi-company — Single ERPNext instance can run 5-10 companies. Inter-company transactions, consolidated financials. Great for groups.
Asset management — Fixed asset register, depreciation (SLM/WDV), asset maintenance, disposal.
POS (Point of Sale) — Offline-capable POS. Works without internet. Syncs when connectivity restored. Suitable for retail.
API-first architecture — Every doctype has REST API. Integrates with any external system (e-commerce, WhatsApp, logistics APIs).
technical: Open-source — No license fees ever. Source code fully available. No vendor lock-in on software.
Self-hosting possible — Run on own server, DigitalOcean, AWS, or own office computer. Full data ownership.
Frappe Framework — Metadata-driven framework. Adding custom fields, doctypes, workflows requires zero code. Low-code extensibility.
Role-based permissions — Granular permission system. Role → Doctype → Field level. User sees only what they should see.
Workflow engine — Approval workflows configurable without code. Purchase Order approval chain, leave application approval, invoice approval — all configurable.
Custom reports — Query Report (SQL), Script Report (Python), Dashboard. Business intelligence built-in. No separate BI tool needed for 80% of MSME reporting needs.
Notifications — Email, SMS, system notifications. Event-driven. 'When Sales Order is submitted, notify warehouse manager'.
Mobile access — Mobile-responsive UI. Works on phone browser. No separate app needed (though PWA available).
Multi-language — 100+ languages. Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi for Indian users. UI language configurable per user.
Print format — Custom invoice/PO/report printing. Company letterhead. GST-compliant tax invoice format out-of-box.
business: Zero license cost — No per-user fee, no module fee, no annual license. Total cost of ownership dramatically lower than SAP/Oracle.
Indian partner ecosystem — 500+ ERPNext partners across India. Tier 1 cities: Multiple options. Tier 2/3 cities: Growing presence.
Frappe Cloud — Managed hosting from Frappe (vendor). Automatic updates, backups, support. ₹3,000-₹15,000/month. No DevOps needed.
Upgrade path — Regular releases (v13→v14→v15). Upgrade script provided. Self-hosters can upgrade. Frappe Cloud upgrades automatically.
No data ransom — Since open-source, data export is always possible. No vendor can hold your data hostage.
Community knowledge base — discuss.frappe.io has solutions to 95% of common problems. YouTube tutorials (Frappe + community). Free learning.
india_specific: GST — Returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B) data available. GST reconciliation. HSN/SAC codes. Tax included/excluded pricing. Composite dealer support.
e-Invoicing — IRN generation via NIC API or GSP. QR code on invoice. Cancellation workflow. Mandatory for turnover >₹5 crore.
e-Way Bill — Generation via API. Vehicle number, transporter. For inter-state shipments >₹50,000.
TDS/TCS — Section-wise TDS deduction. TDS certificate (Form 16A). 26AS reconciliation.
Indian COA — Pre-configured India chart of accounts. State-wise tax accounts.
Indian payroll — PF, ESI, gratuity, bonus, professional tax, LWF. Salary slip in Indian format.
Tally migration — Standard Tally XML export can be imported. Chart of accounts, opening balances, historical data migration support.

usability: UI is functional but not beautiful — Compared to Zoho Books or Odoo, ERPNext UI feels dated. Non-tech users need training. Learning curve: 2-4 weeks to get comfortable.
Overwhelming for very small companies — Full ERPNext has 50+ modules/doctypes visible. For a 5-person company, this is noise. Needs good implementation (hide unused modules) to be manageable.
Mobile UI incomplete — Browser works on mobile, but not optimized. Field-level UX on phone is clunky. No native iOS/Android app (PWA only).
Error messages cryptic — Technical error messages shown to end users. 'LinkValidationError: Cannot delete' is confusing to non-tech user. Implementation partner must handle error documentation.
Reports need customization — Standard reports sufficient for 70% of needs. Remaining 30% needs custom query/script reports. Non-technical users cannot write these themselves.
functional_gaps: No built-in WhatsApp integration — WhatsApp order management not native. Requires third-party integration (ERPNext + WhatsApp Business API). Extra cost + setup.
CRM is weak — ERPNext CRM is basic (Leads, Opportunities, Pipeline). For serious sales teams, Frappe CRM (separate app) or Zoho CRM integration needed.
eCommerce is basic — ERPNext Webshop exists but not competitive with Shopify/WooCommerce. For serious B2C eCommerce, integrate with Shopify (not built-in).
HR/Payroll is adequate, not excellent — For companies >100 employees with complex HR, dedicated HRMS (Keka, Darwinbox) may be preferred alongside ERPNext for ERP.

No Tally-level simplicity for accountants — Tally trained accountants find ERPNext unfamiliar. Voucher entry in Tally = 30 seconds. Same in ERPNext = 2-3 minutes (more fields, validation, workflow). Training mandatory.
Multi-currency limitations — Works for most cases. Complex multi-currency with real-time exchange rates, hedging, forex revaluation needs customization for financial services.
Hospitality/hotel PMS — No property management system. Room booking, housekeeping, restaurant POS integration is weak. Avoid for hotels.
Healthcare — No clinical workflow (OPD, IPD, EMR, prescriptions). Basic invoicing only. Avoid for hospitals/clinics beyond billing.
implementation_risks: Implementation partner quality varies WIDELY — Good partner = smooth implementation. Bad partner = ERPNext blamed for failure. Vetting partner is critical.
Data migration effort underestimated — Cleaning Tally/Excel data for ERPNext import takes 2-4x more time than expected. Dirty data is #1 implementation failure cause.
Customization addiction — 'Just add one more field' accumulates. Heavily customized instances become unmaintainable, hard to upgrade.
Training skipped — Companies rush to go-live, skip training. 3 months later, 20 support tickets all traceable to untrained users.
Process redesign avoided — Company wants ERPNext to match old broken process. Doesn't fix the process. ERP then automates the broken process (garbage in, garbage out).
scale_limits: Very large scale needs tuning — >500 concurrent users, >1 million transactions/month: needs dedicated DBA, server tuning, possibly Elasticsearch for search. Not plug-and-play at scale.
Complex manufacturing — Multi-plant, multi-country, complex shop floor automation (SCADA integration, real-time OEE) needs heavy customization or may need specialized MES.
Retail chains with POS at 100+ locations — ERPNext POS works but scaling to high-frequency POS (1000+ transactions/hour across multiple locations) needs architecture planning.

industries.why: BOM, Work Order, Job Card, Quality Inspection, Subcontracting are all built-in. Best value ERP for manufacturing in sub-₹100 crore revenue segment.
Multi-warehouse, reorder level, lot tracking, price lists, distributor management. India GST for B2B trading built-in.
Project module with task management, timesheet, billing, project profitability. Suitable for CA firms, consultancies, agencies.
Project-based costing with Job Cards. Material issue to project. Scrap tracking. Excellent fit for custom job-based manufacturing.
Batch tracking, expiry date management, FIFO enforcement, quality inspection, India compliance. Food manufacturers find ERPNext well-suited.
POS works well for small retail. Multi-location inventory. But not as smooth as dedicated retail software (POS Nation, RetailEdge). Acceptable for cost-conscious retailers.
industries.caveat: High-frequency POS (>200 transactions/day per location) needs performance testing before go-live.

industries.why: Project module handles project costing. Material management for construction materials works. But no quantity surveyor module, no WBS-level billing, no site-level reporting without customization.
industries.caveat: Construction-specific customization needed. Evaluate Frappe Construction App.

industries.why: Fee collection, accounting work well. Frappe LMS (learning management) is separate app that integrates. Basic student management possible.
industries.caveat: No timetable management, attendance tracking, academic module. Use alongside dedicated EduERP or Fedena for academic functions.

industries.why: Inventory (vehicle stock), service (job card for vehicle servicing), parts trading. Covers basics well.
industries.caveat: No DMS (Dealer Management System) specific features (RC transfer, hypothecation, insurance). Needs customization or dedicated DMS.

industries.why: Batch + expiry tracking for medicine distribution. B2B trading workflows. India GST.
industries.caveat: No Schedule H drug licensing, cold chain management, government tender management. For pharma manufacturers, needs careful evaluation.

industries.why: No clinical workflow (OPD, IPD, prescriptions, lab reports, NABH compliance). ERPNext can handle billing only. Standalone HMIS (HealthPlix, Practo) handles clinical; integration is complex.
industries.recommendation: For billing-only: ERPNext possible. For full hospital: Avoid. Use OpenMRS, HealthPlix.

industries.why: No PMS (property management system). No room inventory, booking engine, housekeeping workflow, channel management, RevPAR reporting.
industries.recommendation: Use dedicated hospitality software (Opera, Hotelogix). ERPNext only for back-office accounting integration.

industries.why: ERPNext webshop not competitive. For high-volume D2C (100+ orders/day), Shopify or WooCommerce is mandatory. ERPNext as backend (inventory, accounting) integrated via API possible.
industries.recommendation: Shopify/WooCommerce → ERPNext integration (ERPNext as ERP backend, not storefront).

industries.why: No loan management system, no trading/settlement workflows, no actuarial functions. Core banking and financial product management not in ERPNext scope.
industries.recommendation: Dedicated NBFC software or Frappe loan management app for simple microfinance. Not suitable for complex financial products.

industries.industry: Very large enterprises (>500 employees, >₹500 crore revenue)
industries.why: Not architectural limitation per se, but support ecosystem, customization complexity, and multi-country compliance at scale pushes towards SAP/Oracle. ERPNext can technically handle but risk increases.
industries.recommendation: ERPNext with very experienced implementation partner possible for ₹200-500 crore range. Beyond that, evaluate SAP Business One.

startup_to_10cr.recommendation: ERPNext is best-in-class for this range. Nothing else offers this depth at this price.
startup_to_10cr.deployment: Frappe Cloud (shared) OR basic self-hosted (DigitalOcean ₹2,000/month server)

10cr_to_100cr.recommendation: Sweet spot. All modules usable, partner ecosystem strong, ROI very clear.
typical_modules: All core + Manufacturing OR Projects + HR

100cr_to_500cr.recommendation: Works well with experienced implementation partner. Heavy customization risk if not managed. Multi-entity, multi-location setups common.
100cr_to_500cr.deployment: Dedicated managed hosting OR private cloud (AWS/Azure). 3-5 server setup.

above_500cr.recommendation: Evaluate carefully. Large Indian companies run on ERPNext successfully but need very experienced team. Consider SAP B1 as alternative if complexity is very high.

single_entity_multi_location.notes: Multi-warehouse, multi-branch cost centers. Standard ERPNext feature.

multi_entity_group.notes: Multi-company setup. Inter-company transactions, consolidated P&L. Works but needs planning.

multi_country.notes: Multi-currency supported. Local compliance (non-India) needs customization. Not first choice for companies with significant overseas operations.

complex_manufacturing_multi_plant.notes: Works with experienced partner. SCADA/MES integration needs custom app development.

implementation_strategy.approach_rationale: ERPNext has many modules. Going live with everything simultaneously causes overwhelm and failure. Phase by module, validate each before moving to next.

phase_1.name: Foundation
phase_1.go_live_readiness: Company can invoice, track stock, manage payables/receivables

phase_2.name: Operations
modules: Manufacturing (BOM, Work Order, Job Card) OR Projects (for service/job shop)
phase_2.go_live_readiness: Production/job tracking live. Cost visibility improving.

phase_3.name: People and Optimization
phase_3.go_live_readiness: Full ERP operational. Analytics and automation running.

critical_success_factors: Strong discovery phase — understand business before configuring anything
Data cleanup before migration — dirty data is #1 failure cause
Owner as champion — without top-level enforcement, staff revert to old methods
Parallel run — keep Tally/Excel running for 1-2 months alongside ERPNext
Training before go-live — not on the job (first live entry should not be training)
Phased go-live — one department/module at a time, not big bang

no_code_customizations: Custom reports (Query Report — SQL, no backend code needed)
Item Groups, Customer Groups, cost centers — all configurable
low_code_customizations: Client scripts (JavaScript — run in browser, auto-fill fields, validate on save)
Server scripts (Python — run on backend, complex validation, automated actions)
requires_developer: Custom apps (new doctype, complex workflow, external API integration)
Third-party API integration (WhatsApp, logistics, eCommerce platforms)
customization_model.customization_risk: Low if done via configuration/scripts. Medium-high if custom apps. High if core Frappe/ERPNext code modified (upgrade breaks customization).
customization_model.recommended_rule: Never modify core code. Always build as separate custom app or via hooks. Keeps upgrade path clean.

from_tally.path: Tally XML export → ERPNext import tool OR Frappe migration scripts. Chart of accounts, opening balances, outstanding invoices, vendor/customer masters.
known_issues: Tally ledger names ≠ ERPNext account naming convention (manual mapping needed)
Multi-currency opening balances need careful handling
Tally narrations don't map 1:1 to ERPNext remarks fields

from_excel.path: ERPNext Data Import tool (CSV upload). Templates available for every doctype. Batch import.
known_issues: Relationship validation — customer must exist before invoice can be imported
Duplicate detection not automatic — must clean Excel first

from_another_erp.path: No one-click migration. Custom scripts needed. REST API available on source (if modern ERP) or CSV export.
known_issues: Doctype mapping between systems (SAP GL → ERPNext Account)
Historical transaction volume may slow import

dirty_data_tolerance.explanation: ERPNext validates data on import. Missing mandatory fields = import fails. Linked record missing = import fails. Data must be cleaned BEFORE import. ERPNext is stricter than Tally (which allows anything).
dirty_data_tolerance.ai_agent_implication: F3 data quality assessment step is CRITICAL before mapping/import. ERPNext will reject dirty data, causing failed imports and user frustration.

master_data_rigidity.explanation: Item must have item_group, stock_uom. Customer must have customer_group, customer_type. Account must have account_type, parent_account. These are mandatory. Can't import partial records.
master_data_rigidity.implication: All master data must be complete before transactional data import.

data_migration_fit.opening_balance_criticality: CRITICAL. Opening stock valuation, opening GL balances, outstanding invoices must be 100% correct on go-live date. Errors here cascade into all future financial reports. This is THE most common point of failure.
migration_risks_ranked: Incorrect opening stock valuation (FIFO/Moving Average — choose before first transaction, can't change after)
Wrong chart of accounts structure (flattening Tally's complex ledger tree into ERPNext's 4-level COA)
Outstanding invoices missing supplier/customer (link validation fails at import time)
Incomplete item master (missing HSN, missing UOM, missing item group)
Fiscal year start date wrong (all transactions in wrong period)

license_cost.note: No per-user licensing. No module licensing. Add 1000 users — zero extra license cost.

hosting_cost.self_hosted_vps: ₹2,000-₹8,000/month (DigitalOcean/AWS VPS, requires Linux admin skill OR outsourced DevOps)
hosting_cost.self_hosted_own_server: ₹0/month cloud (one-time server cost ₹50,000-₹2,00,000, plus electricity, internet, maintenance)

implementation_cost.diy_with_community: ₹0-₹50,000 (time cost only, for tech-savvy users with simple requirements)
implementation_cost.small_partner_msme: ₹1,50,000-₹5,00,000 (for 20-50 person company, standard modules, 6-8 week project)
implementation_cost.experienced_partner_complex: ₹5,00,000-₹20,00,000 (for 50-150 person company, manufacturing or complex multi-module)

ongoing_support_cost.self_managed: ₹0 (community support only — time cost of searching forum, YouTube)
ongoing_support_cost.partner_AMC: ₹10,000-₹50,000/month (implementation partner on annual maintenance contract, issue resolution, minor changes)
ongoing_support_cost.frappe_direct_support: Available for Frappe Cloud enterprise plans

total_cost_of_ownership_3yr_example.scenario: 30-person manufacturing company, Frappe Cloud, experienced partner
total_cost_of_ownership_3yr_example.comparison_sap_b1: SAP B1 equivalent setup = ₹50-80 lakh 3yr TCO

implementation_risk_factors.indicator: Owner says 'we'll adjust ERPNext to our process' without being willing to improve the process
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: Upfront expectation setting. ERPNext works with good processes, not in spite of bad ones.

implementation_risk_factors.indicator: Implementation delegated entirely to one junior staff who has no authority to enforce change
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: Owner or senior manager must be personally involved. Champion needs authority + time.

implementation_risk_factors.risk: Data quality too poor, no cleanup budget
implementation_risk_factors.indicator: Excel with 50% empty fields, 30% duplicates, inconsistent formats
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: Dedicated data cleanup effort (1-4 weeks). Budget for this. F3 data quality assessment step critical.

implementation_risk_factors.indicator: Customer says 'we need to go live in 2 weeks for all modules'
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: Scope to Phase 1 only (Accounts + Stock). Phased approach. Rushing causes panic go-live, data errors, user rejection.

implementation_risk_factors.indicator: Partner is cheap but has no domain knowledge of customer's industry
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: F3 fills this gap. F3 is the implementation intelligence, partner is execution arm.

implementation_risk_factors.indicator: 'Just add one more field' requests every week
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: Document all customizations, prioritize ruthlessly, build only what is essential for go-live.

implementation_risk_factors.indicator: Company wants to 'learn on the job'
implementation_risk_factors.mitigation: Minimum 2 days formal training per department before go-live. Role-specific manuals.

high_risk_company_profiles: Company has never used computers (digital maturity Level 1)
Owner is not involved and has delegated to someone with no authority
Business processes are completely informal (no purchase orders, verbal everything)
Company has had failed ERP implementation before and is skeptical
Company needs ERP live in <4 weeks for complex requirements
Data is entirely on paper (no Excel, no Tally export possible)
low_risk_company_profiles: Currently on Tally, frustrated with lack of manufacturing module
Excel-based with decent discipline (data entry is regular)
Owner is personally driving the ERP initiative
Single location, single product line (limited complexity)
Has tried ERPNext demo, already understands basic concepts

erpnext_wins: Manufacturing module (Tally has none — BOM, Work Order, Job Card not in Tally)
Multi-user collaboration (Tally is single-user legacy architecture)
Process workflow and approvals (Tally has none)
Project costing for job shops
API integration (Tally is closed, hard to integrate)
Cloud-native (Tally is desktop-first)
Inventory management depth (multi-warehouse, batch, serial)
tally_wins: Speed of voucher entry (Tally keyboard-driven, faster for accountants)
Indian CA community familiarity (Tally is industry standard for audit)
GST filing (Tally has deeper Tally.Net integration for direct filing)
Price (Tally Prime: ₹15,000-18,000 one-time. ERPNext implementation: ₹1.5-5 lakh)
vs_tally.recommend_erpnext_over_tally_when: Company needs manufacturing, multi-user, or workflow capabilities. Tally is for accounting only.

erpnext_wins: Manufacturing module (Zoho Books has none — need Zoho Inventory + Zoho Manufacturing separately)
Open source (no vendor lock-in, no license cap risk)
Self-hosting option (data sovereignty)
Deeper inventory (batch, serial, multi-warehouse)
Total cost for large user count (Zoho per-user pricing gets expensive)
zoho_wins: UI/UX superior (Zoho Books is beautiful, modern, intuitive)
Mobile app (native iOS/Android, much better than ERPNext mobile)
Quick setup (Zoho Books live in 1 day. ERPNext: 4-8 weeks)
Zoho suite integration (CRM, Desk, Analytics — seamless if already on Zoho)
Customer support (Zoho has paid support. ERPNext has community + partner)
vs_zoho_books.recommend_erpnext_over_zoho_when: Manufacturing company, or company with >50 users (Zoho per-user cost becomes expensive), or needs deep inventory.

erpnext_wins: India compliance (ERPNext GST/TDS is deeper than Odoo India localization)
Manufacturing depth (ERPNext manufacturing module is more battle-tested for Indian SMEs)
Total cost (Odoo enterprise license expensive. ERPNext free.)
Indian partner ecosystem (ERPNext has larger India-specific partner base)
Community quality for Indian use cases
odoo_wins: App marketplace (Odoo has 30,000+ apps. ERPNext has ~500 community apps)
eCommerce (Odoo eCommerce is production-grade. ERPNext webshop is basic)
HR module (Odoo Payroll is stronger for multi-country)
International compliance breadth (more country localizations than ERPNext)
vs_odoo.recommend_erpnext_over_odoo_when: Indian manufacturing MSME. Budget-conscious. Needs deep India GST compliance without customization.

erpnext_wins: Cost (SAP B1 implementation ₹30-80 lakh. ERPNext ₹2-15 lakh. 5-10x cheaper.)
India MSME suitability (SAP B1 is enterprise-grade, overkill for <₹50 crore revenue)
Implementation speed (ERPNext 8-16 weeks. SAP B1 6-18 months.)
Flexibility without code (ERPNext low-code. SAP B1 needs ABAP developer.)
sap_b1_wins: Brand/credibility (banks, investors, auditors trust SAP more)
Scale (SAP B1 handles >500 users, >5 million transactions reliably)
Multi-country compliance (SAP localizations for 50+ countries are production-grade)
Industry-specific modules (SAP B1 has vertical-specific add-ons)
Support ecosystem (SAP has structured 24/7 support. ERPNext relies on partners.)
vs_sap_b1.recommend_erpnext_over_sap_when: Company is <₹200 crore revenue, Indian operations focus, manufacturing or trading, budget-conscious.

company_red_flags.flag: Owner says 'I want exactly what I have in Excel, but in ERPNext'
company_red_flags.why: This means zero process improvement. ERPNext will be a complex Excel. High failure risk.
company_red_flags.response: Explain: ERPNext requires process adaptation. The goal is better processes, not digital Excel.

company_red_flags.flag: Company has had 2+ failed ERP implementations
company_red_flags.why: Root cause likely organizational (not tool). New tool won't fix organizational resistance.
company_red_flags.response: Deep discovery: Why did previous implementations fail? Address root cause first.

company_red_flags.why: ERPNext overhead (implementation cost, learning curve, maintenance) may not justify ROI at this size.
company_red_flags.response: Suggest: Zoho Books or Vyapar first. Revisit ERPNext at 10+ employees.

company_red_flags.flag: Company is a hospital, hotel, or pure e-commerce
company_red_flags.why: ERPNext poor fit for these industries (no clinical, no PMS, no serious eCommerce).
company_red_flags.response: Recommend specialized software. ERPNext only for back-office accounting if needed.

company_red_flags.flag: Owner is not involved, completely delegated to junior staff
company_red_flags.why: Change management requires authority. Junior staff can't enforce new processes on senior staff.
company_red_flags.response: Require owner commitment before proceeding. Without owner buy-in, expect 60% failure probability.

company_red_flags.flag: Company expects go-live in less than 3 weeks for manufacturing
company_red_flags.why: Manufacturing setup (BOM, operations, workstations, quality) cannot be done properly in <3 weeks. Rushing = bad setup = user rejection.
company_red_flags.response: Minimum 6 weeks for manufacturing go-live (Phase 1 basics). Explain the risk of rushing.

data_red_flags: No data available at all (no Excel, no Tally — purely paper) → Opening stock and master data creation from scratch: 3-6 weeks minimum
Item master has 10,000+ items with duplicate names → Deduplication effort needed before import
Outstanding invoices have no customer name (generic 'Cash Customer') → Can't migrate properly, need cleanup
Multiple currencies used with no exchange rate records → Opening balance reconciliation nightmare

companies_that_succeed_with_erpnext: Manufacturing MSME: 25-60 employees. Owner drives implementation. Clear process (even if manual). Willing to change.
FMCG Distributor: Beat-based sales, multi-warehouse stock. Currently on Tally + Excel hybrid. Frustrated with lack of inventory visibility.
Garment exporter: Size/color variants, BOM-based costing, export compliance. Tally doesn't handle variants.
Food processor: Batch tracking, expiry management, FSSAI compliance documentation. Excel-based is compliance risk.
Job shop (fabrication, printing): Project costing, Job Cards, scrap tracking. No ERP used previously.
Professional services: Project billing, timesheet, multi-project management. Excel losing track of billable hours.
implementation_success_indicators: Owner personally attends all training sessions
Data cleanup completed before implementation start (not during)
Phased go-live (Accounts + Stock first, Manufacturing in Phase 2)
Parallel run for 1-2 months (ERPNext + old system simultaneously for safety)
Weekly review meetings during first 3 months post go-live
Internal champion with time allocated (not 'besides their regular job')

common_failure_modes.description: All modules go live on Day 1. Manufacturing, Accounts, HR, everything simultaneously.
common_failure_modes.outcome: Overwhelmed users, multiple critical issues simultaneously, panic, blame, rollback.
common_failure_modes.prevention: Always phased. Phase 1: Core modules only. Never big bang for first implementation.

common_failure_modes.description: Implementation proceeds without data prep. Data migration started in Week 7 of 8-week project.
common_failure_modes.outcome: Dirty data discovered during import. Delays. Incorrect opening balances. Trust lost.
common_failure_modes.prevention: Data migration prep starts Week 1. Data quality assessment before any configuration.

common_failure_modes.description: ERPNext configured exactly like old broken process. Workflow around existing bad habits.
common_failure_modes.outcome: ERP runs, but same old problems continue in new tool. ROI not realized.
common_failure_modes.prevention: Process review before configuration. Fix broken processes, then configure ERP for fixed process.

common_failure_modes.description: Cost-cutting on training. 'They'll figure it out, it's user-friendly'.
common_failure_modes.outcome: Errors in first month. Support calls spike. Workarounds developed outside system. System abandoned.
common_failure_modes.prevention: Role-specific training (accounting team, warehouse, production). Practice run before go-live.

common_failure_modes.description: Customization requests start Week 2. 'Add this field, change that workflow' while core still not stable.
common_failure_modes.outcome: Scope creep. Project never completes. Customization breaks during upgrade.
common_failure_modes.prevention: Go-live with standard ERPNext. Customization only after 3 months of stable operation. Priority queue.

is_manufacturing_msme.reason: ERPNext manufacturing depth is unmatched in this price range

is_job_shop_fabrication.reason: Project + Job Card workflow maps perfectly to job shop operations

is_india_based.reason: India GST, e-Invoicing, e-Way Bill, TDS built-in. No localization cost.

uses_tally_currently.reason: Tally migration path well-established. Strong Indian Tally community overlap.

needs_manufacturing_module.reason: Manufacturing-specific competitors (Zoho, Tally) lack this depth

revenue_10cr_to_100cr.reason: ERPNext sweet spot. ROI most clear at this revenue range.

batch_expiry_tracking_needed.reason: Batch + expiry tracking is native ERPNext feature (critical for food/pharma)

open_source_preference.reason: Zero license cost, data ownership, customizability — all aligned with open-source preference

project_based_costing_needed.reason: ERPNext Projects module is industry-leading for this price range

multi_warehouse_needed.reason: Native multi-warehouse support with stock ledger per location

very_low_digital_maturity.reason: Company not ready for structured ERP. Needs simpler starting point.

ui_ux_priority_high.reason: ERPNext UI is functional but not beautiful. Zoho/Odoo better if UX is deciding factor.

very_large_enterprise_500plus_employees.reason: Scale risk increases. SAP/Oracle more appropriate at this size.

hospital_or_hotel_industry.reason: ERPNext does not support clinical or PMS workflows. Wrong tool.

pure_ecommerce_dtc.reason: ERPNext eCommerce is weak. Shopify/WooCommerce needed for storefront.

multi_country_complex_compliance.reason: Non-India country localizations in ERPNext are less mature

needs_24_7_paid_support.reason: ERPNext support relies on community + partner. No direct 24/7 SLA from Frappe for standard plans.

owner_resistant_to_process_change.reason: ERPNext requires process discipline. Resistance = implementation failure risk high.

budget_less_than_2_lakh_total.reason: Below ₹2 lakh total budget, can't do proper ERPNext implementation. Suggest Zoho Books or Vyapar.

revenue_below_50_lakh.reason: ROI on ERPNext implementation questionable at very small scale. Simpler tools more appropriate.

scoring_adjustments.scoring_formula: base_score = 0.60 (ERPNext default neutral). final_score = base_score + sum(boost_conditions) + sum(penalty_conditions). Normalize to 0-1. Score > 0.75 = Recommend. Score 0.55-0.75 = Recommend with conditions. Score < 0.55 = Consider alternative.

agent_behavior_hints: When user is manufacturing MSME in India on Tally: ERPNext score will be 0.85+. Recommend confidently.
When user is food processor: Emphasize batch tracking, expiry management, FSSAI documentation via ERPNext. Key differentiator.
When user is job shop: Emphasize Project + Job Card costing. 'Finally know job-wise profitability' is the hook.
When user is trader (FMCG/hardware/auto parts): Emphasize multi-warehouse, price lists, reorder, GST. Beat-based field sales tracking.
When user is very small (< ₹50 lakh revenue, 5 people): Suggest starting with Zoho Books or Vyapar. Revisit ERPNext at ₹1 crore revenue.
When user is hospital or hotel: Do NOT recommend ERPNext. Be honest about limitations. Recommend specialized software.
When owner shows resistance to process change in chatbot conversation: Lower ERPNext score, flag implementation risk prominently.
When user says 'I want everything in 2 weeks': Adjust recommendation to 'ERPNext possible but timeline risky. Start with Phase 1 only.'
data_signals_that_boost_erpnext_score: BOM/recipe files uploaded → Manufacturing depth of ERPNext becomes key value prop
Batch/expiry columns in uploaded data → ERPNext batch tracking fits perfectly
Multiple warehouse/location names → ERPNext multi-warehouse native feature
Job numbers in uploaded data → ERPNext Project module is exact solution
GST columns present → ERPNext India compliance is strong fit
Tally export file detected → Well-established migration path to ERPNext
data_signals_that_lower_erpnext_score: Room/booking/check-in columns → Hotel industry, ERPNext wrong fit
Patient/prescription columns → Hospital industry, ERPNext wrong fit
Only 2-3 employees mentioned → Scale too small for ERPNext overhead
Very high transaction volume (>10,000 transactions/day) → Performance planning needed

consultant_talking_points.opening_value_prop: ERPNext is the most complete, India-ready ERP for manufacturing and trading businesses in the ₹1-100 crore revenue range — and it costs zero in license fees.
consultant_talking_points.cost_comparison: SAP Business One implementation: ₹30-80 lakh. ERPNext implementation: ₹2-8 lakh. Same integrated ERP capability for 10x less cost.
consultant_talking_points.india_advantage: Built in India, by Indians, for Indian businesses. GST, e-Invoicing, TDS — not add-ons. First-class features. Your CA and auditor will recognize the compliance output.
consultant_talking_points.manufacturing_advantage: If you make anything — garments, food, metal parts, anything — ERPNext will tell you: What is this job costing me today? Tally can't do this. Excel can't do this.
consultant_talking_points.honest_limitation: ERPNext is not the simplest software. It will take 4-8 weeks to learn properly. Your team needs to commit. If you want something you can set up in 1 day, Zoho Books is simpler — but it won't give you manufacturing or deep inventory capabilities.
